metadata.title: Poisson, modulus, and eccentricity decomposition audit
metadata.claim_status: Exact periodic/Fourier algebra and logarithmic mass decomposition; method compatibility only, with no asymptotic or new exponential-sum theorem claimed.

starting_point.variables: h=a*u, r=b*v, s=c*w with a,b,c odd, pairwise coprime, and supported on primes 1 mod4
starting_point.parity: v,w odd with arbitrary u, or v,w of opposite parity with even u

deep_terminal_split.log_variables: t=log U=log(B/(a*max(b,c)^2)); the formal main density is t
deep_terminal_split.shallow_fraction: For 0<=tau<=1, the portion with t<=tau*log B is 6*tau^2-8*tau^3+3*tau^4.
deep_terminal_split.terminal_u_split: Within one modulus block, restricting u<=U^(1-sigma) removes exactly a sigma fraction of the harmonic log U main term and forces the shorter original lattice length sqrt(U/u)>=U^(sigma/2).
deep_terminal_split.canonical_choice: With eta=sigma=(log B)^(-1/4), shallow mass is O((log B)^(-1/2)), terminal mass is O((log B)^(-1/4)), and the retained shorter length is at least exp(0.5*sqrt(log B)).
deep_terminal_split.visibility_split: For a slice with original side lengths V,W and D>=1, sum_{d>D} floor(V/d)floor(W/d)<=V*W*sum_{d>D}d^-2<=V*W/(D-1). Taking D as the square root of the retained shorter length makes the large-d tail subexponentially small while leaving both divided side lengths subexponentially large.

parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.visibility: After the parity cases exclude both v,w even, 1_{gcd(v,w)=1}=sum_{d odd, d|v,w}mu(d). The local conditions force gcd(d,b*c)=1.
parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.substitution: v=d*m and w=d*n; use scaled coordinates x=b*d*m and y=c*d*n.
parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.common_period: Both coordinates have the same physical period Q=2*b*c*d.

parity_fourier_coefficients.odd_m_coprime_c: sum over odd r mod 2c with gcd(r,c)=1 equals the Ramanujan coefficient c_{2c}(k)
parity_fourier_coefficients.even_m_coprime_c: sum over even r mod 2c with gcd(r,c)=1 equals c_c(k)

parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.poisson_formula: For a smooth sector weight W_R, one parity class equals Q^-2 * sum_{k,l} A_c(k)A_b(l) * hat(W_R)(k/Q,l/Q), Q=2bcd.
parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.zero_frequency: A_c(0)=phi(c) and A_b(0)=phi(b) in every parity class; combining the odd-odd class with the two opposite-parity/even-u classes recovers the two-adic factor fixed in Stage12-N1-2f.
parity_local_coprimality_fourier_algebra.consequence: The previously anisotropic b/c ellipse is converted, in the full two-dimensional periodic formulation, into a fixed circular sector with an isotropic dual denominator Q. The arithmetic complexity moves into Ramanujan coefficients.

dual_phase.fourier_decay_framework: After smoothing and stationary phase for the curved circular boundary, a nonzero frequency has oscillation with radial parameter Z=(R/Q)*sqrt(k^2+l^2).
dual_phase.u_dependence: Since R is proportional to sqrt(B/a)*u^(-1/2), the phase is exp(plus_or_minus const*sqrt(B/a)*sqrt(k^2+l^2)/(b*c*d*sqrt(u))).
dual_phase.second_derivative_test: For sum_{u~U} exp(A*u^(-1/2)), van der Corput gives O(A^(1/2)U^(-1/4)+A^(-1/2)U^(5/4)) =O(Z^(1/2)+U*Z^(-1/2)), where Z=A/sqrt(U).
dual_phase.status: This supplies per-frequency cancellation when Z is large, but it does not by itself sum the two-dimensional frequencies, Ramanujan weights, and b,c,d blocks.

leading_log_mass_zones.coordinates: Assume b<=c and write y=log b, z=log c, t=log(B/(a*c^2)); subpower d and smoothing shifts do not change leading fractions.

zones.name: A_separated_two_dimensional_core
zones.method_status: Adjacent reciprocal moduli have phase separation R/Q^2>=1 at the lowest radial frequency, so an additive-spacing or hybrid argument is structurally plausible.

zones.name: B_clustered_two_dimensional_core
zones.method_status: Two-dimensional Poisson remains oscillatory, but adjacent q values are unresolved at low radial frequency; a nonlinear spacing/additive-energy estimate is required.

zones.name: C_one_dimensional_eccentric_wing
zones.method_status: The common-period two-dimensional Poisson series contains many low frequencies. Return to the original anisotropic lattice and apply one-dimensional Poisson or a sawtooth expansion in the long direction.

large_sieve_compatibility.spacing_resolution: On u~U, two moduli q,q' are distinguishable at radial frequency sqrt(m) only when R*sqrt(m)*abs(1/q-1/q') is at least order 1. For adjacent q~Q and m=1 this is R/Q^2.
large_sieve_compatibility.ordinary_additive_large_sieve: Direct spacing therefore naturally covers Q<=sqrt(R), the 9/32 zone, but not the 15/32 clustered core.
large_sieve_compatibility.kloosterman_or_spectral_large_sieve: Known Kloosterman large-sieve and Kloosterman-fraction estimates exploit modular inverses or genuine Kloosterman sums.  The present phase is a continuous reciprocal square-root phase with Ramanujan coefficients, so those theorems do not apply verbatim.
large_sieve_compatibility.monomial_exponential_sums: After dyadic decomposition the phase belongs to a multivariable monomial/reciprocal family. Robert-Sargos-type or later monomial estimates are plausible inputs, but existing work also shows that applying dyadic-box monomial estimates mechanically can be insufficient in critical ranges.
large_sieve_compatibility.required_new_bound: A weighted nonlinear hybrid inequality for sum lambda_1(b)lambda_1(c)mu(d) A_c(k)A_b(l) exp(C*sqrt(k^2+l^2)/(b*c*d*sqrt(u))), with a separate one-dimensional estimate for Q>R.

literature_audit.work: Brandolini-Travaglini, Fourier analytic techniques for lattice point discrepancy, arXiv:1909.03439
literature_audit.usable_part: Poisson/Fourier and stationary-phase framework for planar convex-body discrepancy.
literature_audit.gap: Does not provide the required b,c,d,u-weighted Ramanujan hybrid estimate.

literature_audit.work: Drappeau, Sums of Kloosterman sums in arithmetic progressions, arXiv:1504.05549
literature_audit.usable_part: Power-saving technology for multilinear genuine Kloosterman sums with congruence variables.
literature_audit.gap: The Stage12 dual phase has no modular inverse or genuine Kloosterman kernel.

literature_audit.work: Bettin-Chandee, Trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, arXiv:1502.00769
literature_audit.usable_part: Strong bounds for reciprocal phases containing modular inverses.
literature_audit.gap: Its kernel e(a*inverse(m)/n) is structurally different from sqrt(k^2+l^2)/(b*c*d*sqrt(u)).

literature_audit.work: Pliego, Estimates for a three-dimensional exponential sum with monomials, arXiv:2211.02096
literature_audit.usable_part: Van der Corput, stationary phase, exponent-pair, and monomial-sum comparison tools.
literature_audit.gap: The paper itself records parameter ranges where generic dyadic-box monomial estimates are not satisfactory; the Stage12 weights and radial frequency require a dedicated budget.

closed: Shallow height, terminal u, and large visibility-divisor ranges admit an o(main) cutoff architecture.
Parity and both local coprimality conditions can be Fourier-combined into a common square period Q=2bcd.
The exact leading-log mass splits into 9/32 separated core, 15/32 clustered core, and 1/4 one-dimensional wing.
The dual exponential phase and the precise large-sieve spacing barrier Q=sqrt(R) are explicit.
not_closed: Summation of stationary-phase amplitudes and Ramanujan coefficients with lambda_1 weights.
A raw error of power-saving size or O(B*(log B)^(2-eta)).
decision.next_stage: 12-N1-2i: derive exponent-pair and Ramanujan-second-moment budgets for the 15/32 clustered core and the 1/4 one-dimensional wing; decide whether the concrete Poisson sums can meet the primitive-error target.

not_claimed: A proved raw or primitive asymptotic.
That the large-d and smoothing budgets have been written with final sharp constants.
That existing Kloosterman or monomial theorems cannot be adapted after further transformations.
That zone A is already closed; only structural compatibility and spacing are established.
